RESEARCH BRIEF / IMPLICATIONS FOR HNB
Draft: 17 September 2026 | Author review pending
1 / 2
HNB in Croatia’s inflation debate
More attention to prices need not mean more attention to the central
bank.
The paper asks whether the Croatian National Bank’s (HNB) relative media visibility keeps pace when inflation
dominates the news. Its contribution is to separate what the institution publishes from its place in the wider
debate. Higher inflation accompanies a smaller institutional share in the primary models; visibility declines during
April 2024-May 2026.
READING THE INDICATOR
Relevance selects items about inflation. Prominence reflects the institution’s presence in the title, position and
frequency of mentions, and cues that it acts or speaks. The measure combines prominence with potential reach and
compares this with reach across inflation coverage. The attention gap = baseline share minus current weighted
share. A larger gap means less relative visibility.
Example: a 4% baseline and a 3% current share give a +1 percentage-point gap. These are illustrative values. The
baseline is a historical reference, not a communication target; the share is neither readership nor a simple percentage of
articles.
THE SCALE OF THE INFLATION ASSOCIATION
Inflation from 2% to 10%: a 1.68 percentage-point lower weighted share. Holding the other variables fixed,
the primary weekly model implies a weighted share lower by the same amount (95% interval: 0.90 to 2.46). This
is the paper’s conditional comparison, not a forecast or a policy effect.
How robust? Per 1 percentage point higher inflation, the primary gap estimate is 0.21 pp (95% interval 0.11 to 0.31;
268 fitted weeks). All three chart models include media volume. With year effects, the interval includes zero; the
association is not independent of every choice of time controls. The monthly trend-control model is also inconclusive.
Source: paper Section 4.2 and Appendix A23. HICP is the Harmonised Index of Consumer Prices; inflation is the year-on-year rate.

RESEARCH BRIEF / IMPLICATIONS FOR HNB
Draft: 17 September 2026 | Author review pending
2 / 2
What the findings mean for HNB
1. Assess visibility after the inflation surge as well. Within April 2024-May 2026, the controlled gap trend is
+0.076 pp per month (95% interval 0.035 to 0.118; 25 fitted months). Keeping only common sources still gives
+0.056 pp per month (p = 0.045). This is evidence of declining relative visibility within that period, not proof that
disinflation caused the decline.
2. Distinguish visibility from network position. A share describes how much of the debate the institution
occupies. Centrality describes its position among actors linked through media sources, weighting connections to
well-connected actors more heavily. The common-source monthly trend is -0.0051 index units (95% interval -0.0129
to 0.0027; p = 0.187). The interval includes zero: lasting structural erosion is not established.
3. Read media evidence alongside expectations surveys. For the article-share measure, baseline weekly
projections find no significant future horizons with linear survey interpolation, but weeks 1-2 with step assignment;
the monthly comparison finds month 12, after correction for multiple tests. Controls change the pattern too. These
results do not establish a stable predictive channel, or show that a media gap causes expectations to become
unanchored.
Implication for the governor. Consider institutional output, relative media representation and public understanding
as separate dimensions. More publications need not produce a larger share of a growing debate. The gap adds a
diagnostic of representation; it does not score message quality, credibility or policy success.
SCOPE AND SOURCE
January 2021-May 2026: 60 monthly / 268 weekly observations in the main regressions. Generic central-bank terms may include the
ECB or others; potential reach is not observed exposure. The selected corpus is not a representative audience sample. Earlier-paper
numerical discrepancies remain unresolved.
Petra Palić and Luka Sikić | Hrvatsko katoličko sveučilište. Independent draft, 17 September 2026; not an HNB publication. Sections
4.2-4.7, discussion, Appendices A12, A23 and B2. Figures and numbers use saved results; models were not re-estimated.
